                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>' where
                REGION is the region derived from the owner's postcode (or
                'UNKNOWN' when the postcode maps to no known region) and HASH8 is
                the first 8 upper-case hex characters of the SHA-256 of the
                normalized (E.164) telephone concatenated with the lastName.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-3C1A9F2B'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>'
                where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-3C1A9F2B-M26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable shared identifier for the owner's household, derived
                deterministically as the first 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 of
                the normalized lastName and postcode. Every owner sharing the same
                lastName and postcode is assigned the same householdId
                automatically.
              type: string
              example: '3C1A9F2B7D4E'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that, at the time this owner was
                created, already shared the same firstName and lastName
                (compared case-insensitively).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-

                creation: it starts at 1, gains 1 when an email is present, gains
                1 when namesakeCount is 0, and is capped at 3. Level 4 is reserved
                for tenure.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality: the '<REGION>' component of the
                customerCode (its prefix up to the first '-'), i.e. the region
                derived from the owner's postcode at creation, or 'UNKNOWN' when
                the postcode maps to no known region.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:

                had already been created for the same day. True once the daily
                total exceeds 80, otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: >-
                The owner's preferred contact channel: 'EMAIL' when an email is
                present, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The single derived key used for duplicate detection: the
                normalized (E.164) telephone, the email (lower-cased, or empty
                when absent) and the householdId (or empty when the owner has no
                household), joined with '|'. Two owners are duplicates, and the
                second is rejected with 409, only when their whole identity keys
                are equal.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|jane@example.test|3C1A9F2B7D4E'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-

                decimal digits contained in the owner's customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 7
              readOnly: true
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: >-

                registrationDate: 'MINOR' when under 18, 'ADULT' from 18 to 64,
                and 'SENIOR' at 65 or older. Absent when no birthDate is given.
              type: string
              example: 'ADULT'

              title: Possible duplicate

                owner's lastName and postcode with a different telephone. The

              example: false

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1

    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '[\s\S]*\S[\s\S]*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '[\s\S]*\S[\s\S]*'
          example: Madison

          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept when present,
            otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'

          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email

          maxLength: 255

            registrationDate.

            digits and valid for the owner's city per the fixed region ranges

            region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned when given.

              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:

                REGION is the region derived from the owner's postcode (or
                'UNKNOWN' when the postcode maps to no known region) and HASH8 is
                the first 8 upper-case hex characters of the SHA-256 of the
                normalized (E.164) telephone concatenated with the lastName.

              readOnly: true

              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID

                deterministically as the first 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 of
                the normalized lastName and postcode. Every owner sharing the same
                lastName and postcode is assigned the same householdId

                creation: it starts at 1, gains 1 when an email is present, gains
                1 when namesakeCount is 0, and is capped at 3. Level 4 is reserved
                for tenure.

              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 3
              readOnly: true

                customerCode (its prefix up to the first '-'), i.e. the region
                derived from the owner's postcode at creation, or 'UNKNOWN' when
                the postcode maps to no known region.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true

              readOnly: true
            identityKey:

                normalized (E.164) telephone, the email (lower-cased, or empty
                when absent) and the householdId (or empty when the owner has no
                household), joined with '|'. Two owners are duplicates, and the
                second is rejected with 409, only when their whole identity keys
                are equal.
              type: string

              readOnly: true

              readOnly: true

            possibleDuplicateOf:

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
          required:

## Summary

The spec asked for a new read-only `telephoneDisplay` field: the stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans (e.g. `+61412345678` → `+61 412 345 678`), while keeping `telephone` as raw E.164.

Two edits, following the codebase's existing derived-field pattern:

1. **`Owner.java`** — added a `getTelephoneDisplay()` derived getter. It strips the leading `+`, resolves the country calling code via the existing `countryCodeOf(...)` helper (reusing the single source of the country-code table), then emits `+<cc> <national digits grouped in threes>`. It defensively returns the telephone unchanged when it's `null`, not E.164, or carries no known country code.

2. **`openapi.yml`** — added a `telephoneDisplay` `readOnly` string property to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gains the field and MapStruct auto-maps it from `owner.getTelephoneDisplay()` (same mechanism as `displayName`, `initials`, etc.).

The raw `telephone` remains untouched (still normalized to/stored as E.164).

Results: `AcceptanceTest.coreFormatsTelephoneDisplay` passes — `$.telephone` = `+61412345678`, `$.telephoneDisplay` = `+61 412 345 678` — and the full `mvn test` run is `BUILD SUCCESS` with all tests green.
